meaning: A starchy root vegetable eaten cooked, like a large potato
examples: A bowl of udon with grated yam on top, please.
She baked a sweet yam for dinner.

meaning: Talking loudly and continuously, often complaining (informal)
trick: YAMMER — 'yam yam yam' — mouth never stops.
examples: All this constant yammering about dying...
Stop yammering and help me.
He yanked the rope free from her hand.
She yanked the door open.
Laila found Mariam yanking drawers open and slamming them shut.
Stop yanking the dog's lead.

meaning: Pulls something or someone suddenly and hard
examples: Laila yanks her children back onto the sidewalk.
He yanks the blanket off the bed.

meaning: Units of length (about 0.9 metres); here, a large amount of cloth
trick: YARD – about one long step; yards of cloth = lots of it.
examples: The yards of pleated cloth spilled over his knees.
She bought three yards of silk for the dress.

usage.pattern: yards of + something / a hundred yards

meaning: Long thread of wool or cotton used for knitting or weaving; also (informal) a long, often made-up story
hindi: ऊन का धागा, सूत; लंबी कहानी
trick: YARN = what you knit on a rainy day when you YAwN at home.
examples: Kaka Zaman kept knitting needles and balls of yarn ready.
My grandmother bought red yarn to knit a sweater.

usage.pattern: a ball of yarn / knit something with yarn

meaning: Opened the mouth wide and breathed in deeply because tired or bored
trick: YAWNED = YAWN at dawn: too sleepy, mouth wide open.
examples: Just then I yawned, and the old man said he'd better make a move.
She yawned during the long meeting.

meaning: Very wide and open, like a gap or hole; also opening the mouth wide because tired
hindi: चौड़ा खुला, गहरा; जम्हाई लेता हुआ
trick: YAWNING hole = a hole open as wide as a big YAWN.
examples: The old factory wall was pocked with yawning holes from the shelling.
There is a yawning gap between the rich and the poor.

meaning: To want something very strongly, especially something hard to get
trick: YEARN ≈ 'year' → waiting a whole year for something you long for.
examples: Enough to make her yearn for death.
Many city people yearn for a quiet life.

usage.pattern: yearn for something / yearn to do something

meaning: Shouted loudly, often in anger or excitement
examples: I get yelled at for not bracing my stomach.
She yelled at the kids to stop running.

usage.pattern: yell at someone / get yelled at

meaning: A short, sharp, high cry of pain, fear or surprise
trick: YELP = a quick YELL for helP.
examples: She let out a high-pitched yelp.
The puppy gave a yelp when I stepped on its tail.

usage.pattern: let out / give a yelp (of pain/surprise)

meaning: Short, sharp, high cries of pain or fear
trick: YELPS = many little YELLs for helP.
examples: Then it was all dust and kicks and yelps.
We heard yelps from the dogs playing in the yard.

meaning: Two opposite things that go together and complete each other (from Chinese philosophy)
trick: The black-and-white circle symbol: two opposite halves make one whole.
examples: These are the yin and yang of any toxic relationship: the victim and the saver.
My brother and I are yin and yang: he is loud and I am quiet.

usage.pattern: the yin and yang of something / be yin and yang
partners: the yin and yang of life

meaning: The plural of "yourself"; used when "you" means more than one person
hindi: आप लोग स्वयं, तुम सब खुद
examples: Prostrate yourselves.
Help yourselves to some snacks, kids.

usage.pattern: help yourselves / enjoy yourselves / by yourselves

examples: Isn't it mind-bogglingly yummy?
This chocolate cake is so yummy!
